children: Meta Platforms Inc. (META, Financials), the social media firm that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has invested large sums of money on artificial intelligence. Now investors are receiving something they can really try.

Meta shares gained almost 5% on Wednesday as Wall Street responded to Muse, the company's latest personal AI assistant. Muse can help users buy, organize trips, write emails and manage everyday tasks. That sounds easy enough but time is important.
Investors have seen Meta spend billions on AI infrastructure. What they've wanted is a product that could someday transform all that expense into revenue. And Muse might be that product.

Mizuho called the launch an important step in that direction. KeyBanc reiterated its price target at $780 and said Meta's AI opportunity may still be underappreciated. And unlike most AI firms, Meta has something else: distribution.

It can put Muse in front of users across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger without having to cultivate an audience from the ground up. But a good launch is not enough. Meta has produced grand items previously that didn't live up to the hype.

The next test for investors is a simple one: Will customers continue to use Muse beyond the first excitement? But if engagement holds, Meta could finally have a clearer path to turning its AI spending into another growth engine.

title: Meta's New AI Agent Just Gave Wall Street Something It Wanted
